title: No Pilots. Few Air Traffic Controllers. What Could Go Wrong?
gist: Jeff Wise examines AI's fast entry into conservative aviation: the FAA's AI-powered SMART tool (by Air Space Intelligence) amid a national groundstop and cut controller staffing targets, Joby's pilotless 3,200-mile Cessna flight and S4 eVTOL demos under eIPP, and Amazon/Walmart drone-delivery expansion — weighed against pilot-union resistance and AI reliability and hallucination risks.

insights.claim: The FAA deployed SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories), an AI air traffic management tool built by Boston-based Air Space Intelligence, announced in September 2026 by transportation secretary Sean Duffy as a 'GAME CHANGER'.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Air Space Intelligence is a direct beneficiary of federal ATC modernization spend; SMART's track record will shape future AI procurement.

insights.claim: About three weeks after SMART's promotion, the FAA issued a national groundstop on Friday the 13th over a communications failure; officials said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or SMART involvement, but Homeland Security secretary Markwayne Mullin would not definitively rule out AI failure.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Unresolved causes of a national groundstop raise headline and regulatory risk for AI-in-aviation vendors and airline schedules.
insights.locator: Almost three weeks later, that post

insights.claim: Almost two dozen Democratic lawmakers reportedly asked the Government Accountability Office on October 13 to review SMART, citing fears it might hallucinate safety-critical information.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Congressional oversight could slow or condition AI ATC deployments; watch for GAO findings.
insights.locator: Some lawmakers are also concerned about SMART

insights.claim: In May the FAA cut its staffing target for active air traffic controllers from the 2024 goal of 14,633 to 12,563, citing modern staffing models and scheduling tools, raising concern that AI efficiency is being used to justify workforce reduction amid a chronic controller shortage.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Lower controller targets justified by AI tools increase operational fragility if the software underdelivers; a risk for airline reliability.
insights.locator: In May, the FAA reduced its staffing target

insights.claim: A recently retired FAA employee warns that the rush of new ATC technology, which he calls the 'Trump/DOGE/Musk effect', ignores the complexity of the national airspace system and will be a disaster.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Insider skepticism signals implementation risk in AI ATC rollouts that markets may underprice.
insights.quote: “This is literally a Pandora's box that we are going to regret.”

insights.claim: Supporters such as former DOT inspector general Mary Schiavo and Embry-Riddle professor Michael McCormick see predictive trajectory tools like SMART as an improvement, since detecting conflicts earlier means less effort to resolve them.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Predictive conflict detection is the near-term, lower-risk value case for AI in ATC.
insights.quote: the sooner you know about a potential conflict, the less effort is required to resolve it.
insights.locator: Michael McCormick, a professor of air traffic management

insights.claim: Joby Aviation flew a Cessna Caravan 3,200 miles coast to coast, from Concord, California to North Carolina via Phoenix, Fort Worth and South Carolina, navigating busy airspace and storms without a human touching the controls; a safety pilot aboard never intervened.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Demonstrated long-range autonomy strengthens Joby's position in pilotless flight, the key to eVTOL unit economics.
insights.quote: The entire journey took place without a single human hand touching the plane’s controls.
insights.locator: None of this would be remarkable

insights.claim: Joby's S4 eVTOL, unveiled in 2020 to carry a pilot and four passengers 100+ miles at up to 200 mph, flew the first point-to-point eVTOL flight within New York City in April, from JFK to three Manhattan heliports, under the federal eVTOL Integration Pilot Program (eIPP).
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: eIPP gives Joby a regulatory pathway to demonstration and eventually paid passenger flights; a catalyst to track.
insights.locator: Joby and other eVTOL companies haven’t progressed

insights.claim: The eIPP rollout path runs from demo flights to nonpaying-passenger flights, then paying-passenger demos, then A-to-B passenger service, all with increasing oversight.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Each eIPP stage is a milestone for eVTOL commercialization timelines and valuation.

insights.claim: eVTOL economics require eventual autonomy, because paying a human pilot to fly a handful of passengers is too expensive for the model to make sense.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Air-taxi profitability hinges on regulatory acceptance of pilotless flight; piloted launches are not the end-state business.
insights.quote: for the model to make any economic sense, the aircraft will have to fly themselves.
insights.locator: To start, these flights will have human pilots

insights.claim: By 2022 there were 600 eVTOL models under development, but commercial launches kept slipping because airspace design, pilot/supervisor training and economic frameworks also had to be built.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: A crowded field facing slipping timelines implies consolidation; regulatory and airspace progress matters as much as aircraft engineering.
insights.locator: A commercial launch seemed just around the corner.

insights.claim: Amazon plans to expand drone delivery to 500 US locations by end of 2026 and Walmart plans drone delivery from 270 stores by end of 2027, aided by FAA beyond-visual-line-of-sight waivers since 2023 that could become a permanent rule change by year end.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: A permanent BVLOS rule would unlock scaled drone logistics, benefiting Amazon, Walmart and drone suppliers.

insights.claim: DroneUp COO Anthony Vittone predicts drone delivery will be completely ubiquitous in five to 10 years, with a maximal build-out of hundreds of thousands of drones serving most of the US population.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Bullish industry TAM framing for drone logistics; verify against actual rollout pace.
insights.quote: “In five to 10 years, it’s going to be completely ubiquitous,”
insights.locator: The ultimate goal is far larger.

insights.claim: Google's Project Wing, unveiled in 2014 and serving 164 homes near Canberra by 2018, was not meant to be viable but to build operational experience; the 2007 NextGen program's ADS-B mandate by 2020 laid the groundwork for robot-friendly skies.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Early loss-making pilots buy operating know-how; incumbents with long programs have a head start.
insights.locator: With a road map to robot-friendly skies

themes.theme: Pilot resistance and AI reliability limits

insights.claim: Airbus and Dassault asked EASA in 2017 to allow single-pilot airliner operations with automation as copilot; after strong protest from the European Cockpit Association pilots' union, EASA shelved the plan last year.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Labor resistance can block cockpit-crew reduction, limiting near-term airline cost savings from automation.
insights.locator: AI faced another kind of resistance in Europe.

insights.claim: AI's near-term entry into passenger aviation will be behind-the-scenes data software, with Palantir, Jeppesen and Thales selling AI tools to regulators, airlines and dispatchers for risk identification and crew/aircraft scheduling.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Aviation analytics software vendors are the lower-risk near-term winners from AI in aviation.
insights.locator: Given the scale of the challenge

insights.claim: Aviation AI research focuses on deterministic neural networks with frozen weights that cannot hallucinate, but Collins Aerospace researcher Darren Cofer noted they can produce unexpected and potentially dangerous outputs in situations unseen in training.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Certification of AI flight systems will hinge on out-of-distribution safety, a likely bottleneck for autonomy timelines.
insights.locator: That sounds great, but building machines

insights.claim: Real-time AI air traffic control will likely begin in dedicated corridors near drone hubs and eVTOL vertiports, because traditional ATC would be overwhelmed by the volume of autonomous aircraft, per Michael McCormick.
insights.speaker: Jeff Wise
insights.so_what: Segregated autonomous airspace creates a new market for AI traffic-management providers ahead of mainstream ATC.
insights.quote: it would overwhelm the national airspace system if it tried to handle that volume and complexity of airframes moving around.
insights.locator: The stakes will be even higher
